title: Davis voters opposing Village Farms with more ballots to count - Abridged – PBS KVIE
content: If approved, Measure V would add up to 1,800 residential units just west of the Wildhorse neighborhood. Early returns show more than half of counted ballots in Davis opposing Measure V. If approved, the measure would give the green light to the Village Farms development. With about 30% of registered votes counted, the “yes” campaign had 48% of the vote as of midnight, while “no” had 52%. To move ahead, the project would need a simple majority, or 51%, of Davis voters to approve it. Measure V’s approval would add up to 1,800 residential units just west of the Wildhorse neighborhood. If voters reject it, the project will not move forward, and the approval process would need to restart for any future proposal. While early results show a majority of votes opposing the measure, the election will not be certified until all votes are counted and, so far, it’s a close race. The county will continue to share updates, with the next batch of results expected Friday. The ballot measure, which the Davis City Council approved in January, has faced ongoing scrutiny from opponents who have a list of environmental concerns and worries over its potential effects on traffic and public health. Supporters point to a city-approved environmental impact report that they say addresses many of these concerns. They also highlight sagging enrollment at Davis schools and increasingly unaffordable housing. This isn’t the first time a housing development on this piece of land has been proposed. In 2005, Davis voters rejected Covell Village by just under 4,000 votes. That project, which had a similar footprint to Village Farms, attracted much of the same opposition and eventually failed. Another project on Davis’ northern boundary will be on the ballot this November. The Davis City Council approved the Willowgrove proposal, which would bring 1,250 new units to Davis, in early May. title: Obituary for Marcella Diane (Nail) Sapp - Ronald V. Hall Funeral Home
content:

                    can stop at any time. Your email will not be used for any other purpose. Marcella Diane Sapp, 58, entered into eternal rest on June 1, 2026, at Community Hospice. Born on July 8, 1967, Marcella was the daughter of Velma Beasley Curl of Reidsville and Ben L. Nail of Collins. She was a 1985 graduate of Pinewood Christian Academy and knew from an early age that she was called to become a teacher. She attended Georgia Southern University, where she earned both her Bachelor of Science and Master of Science degrees in Early Childhood Education. Marcella devoted her life to teaching and nurturing young minds. During her career, she taught in the Tattnall, Montgomery, and Wheeler County school systems. Although she never had children of her own, she lovingly considered her students to be her children. She poured her heart into the classroom and touched the lives of countless students and their families through her compassion, patience, and dedication. A faithful member of First Baptist Church of Lyons, Marcella’s life was grounded in her Christian faith. Shortly after beginning her teaching career, she married the love of her life, William “Lee” Sapp of Lyons. Together they shared more than thirty-one years of marriage built on faith, love, laughter, and unwavering devotion. In November 2004, Marcella was diagnosed with a benign brain tumor, a diagnosis that ultimately prevented her from returning to the classroom she loved so dearly. Through every challenge that followed, Lee remained faithfully by her side, honoring the vows he made before God. Despite the limitations imposed by her illness, Marcella and Lee continued to enjoy road trips and make cherished memories together for many years. In January 2023, Marcella’s health declined further, leaving her bedridden. Yet even then, her mind remained as sharp as ever. She enjoyed talking on the phone with family and friends, sharing good food, and watching her favorite television programs. Though her earthly body endured many hardships, Marcella rarely complained. Those closest to her knew that if she voiced her struggles, it was in prayer. In her Bible, she had marked Psalm 143, a quiet testimony to the faith that sustained her through difficult days. Though she seldom shared her burdens with others, she faithfully carried them to the Lord in prayer. Marcella will be remembered for her loving heart, her dedication to education, her quiet strength, and her steadfast faith in God. Her grace in the face of adversity was an inspiration to all who knew her. She was preceded in death by her stepmother, Kay Lively Nail; her brother-in-law, Dewey O. Batton; and her grandparents, Otis and Jessie Beasley and Frank and Eunice Nail. Left to cherish her memory are her devoted husband of more than thirty-one years, William “Lee” Sapp; her beloved fur babies; her mother and stepfather, Velma and Gary Curl of Reidsville; her father, Ben L. Nail of Collins; her sister, Melissa Batton of Lyons; her brother, Brent Nail (MaryLynn) of Bishop; her niece, Laura Johnson of Lebanon, Tennessee; her nephew, Ben Johnson of Atlanta; her nephew, Garrett Nail, and her niece, Gracen Nail, both of Bishop; her great-nephews, Camdon Cody and Carson Cody of Lebanon, Tennessee; and numerous extended family members, former students, and dear friends. A graveside funeral service celebrating Marcella’s life will be held on Saturday morning, June 6th, 2026, at 10:00 at Cedar Creek Primitive Baptist Church, 1199 Cedar Creek Church Road, Collins, Georgia. Pastor Brian Durden will officiate. Pallbearers are Brent Nail, Garrett Nail, James Rogers, Joe Skeens, Ben Johnson, and Tommy Kennedy. Flowers will be accepted, or memorial contributions may be made to Community Hospice Foundation, PO Box 2277, Vidalia, GA 30475, in Marcella’s memory. Though she is no longer with us, Marcella’s legacy lives on in the lives she touched, the students she inspired, and the family and friends who were blessed to know and love her. “Well done, good and faithful servant.” — Matthew 25:23 To send flowers
